body:
@stefanbucur Does using "" instead of None work for you?
This is a bug either way. I'm just trying to understand severity so we can prioritize.

> @stefanbucur Does using "" instead of None work for you?

Using `""` shows a different error:

```
ERROR: [...]/bazel-rules-fuzzing/fuzzing/private/instrument.bzl:33:5: IllegalArgumentError for option 'copt': Can not set java.util.List field com.google.devtools.build.lib.rules.cpp.CppOptions.coptList to java.lang.String
ERROR: Errors encountered while applying Starlark transition
```

However, it does work when I use a list type instead (`[]`), presumably because `--copt` are list-typed command-line options.

My bad. I should have said [] rather than "".
Thanks for checking. With an easy workaround, we know better how to prioritize it.

(Context: I'm moving on from Bazel on friday and spending some time triaging all bugs assigned to me before unassigning myself)

Both //command_line_option:copt and //command_line_option:linkopt should use `[]` instead of None to indicate an empty value since they are stored as [List types](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/cpp/CppOptions.java;l=321?q=CppOptions.java&ss=bazel). Yes, we should change the code such that it doesn't NPE though.

Hey, newbie here - I've seen this has been marked as a good first issue, so I'm happy to pick this up. If you can let me know what the expectation is for the resolution of this issue, that'll be great e.g a more useful exception message rather than an NPE? Or some sensible defaults?

In addition, if you can point me to an area of code where I can start poking around that'll be appreciated (I'll also dig through the stack trace).

Thanks!

My $0.02 (not on the Bazel team, so deferring the decision on the semantics here to them): I think it would be nice if Bazel would show a compilation error when using the `None` value for any configuration value in the transition output. It currently hard-crashes with a Java exception.

Hi @tobiade -  I just saw this thread. Happy you're interested in contributing! First and foremost, have you gone through the basics of simply building Bazel? Like make a trivial change (to a string or something) and verify you can build and run a custom Bazel with it?

Happy to offer more input on this particular issue from that point. I'll have to review the thread to remember details, but can definitely better scope the issue.

Thanks! @gregestren - I've been able to successfully build [Bazel from source](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/install-compile-source.html), but been having a bit of a nightmare trying to get Bazel set up in Intellij on Windows using the Intellij plugin. I did eventually find out that the plugin isn't supported on Windows, so I'm looking for a workaround now e.g WSL2 + IntelliJ.

Sorry about the IntelliJ problems. I haven't had any issues on Linux, so hopefully that approach works.

The core issue, I believe, is there are different kinds of data typing in Bazel. When you set a value to `None`, you're setting it to a type in the Starlark language. Transitions ultimately set that to pure Java types. For example, `copt` is [ultimately](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/2d28044316bf1ea9935f85e9a6876062abce169f/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/cpp/CppOptions.java#L278) a Java `List<String>`.

I think the specific code doing this translation is at https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/98d376faeb206f14838156ce4cb305ddbfce08fa/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/analysis/starlark/FunctionTransitionUtil.java#L297-L299 So this may be a matter of examining the option's type, and if it's a list type, change it to `[]` instead of `null`?

An alternative approach could be to ban setting values to `None`, so examples like the above simply report "This is not a valid assignment`.  With that approach, maybe the same  would trigger an error message instead of trying to change the conversion. 

But for non-list types, setting to `None` makes more sense. So maybe the first approach is more consistent.

Is that enough to work with?
Hey! Sorry about the delay - thanks, that makes sense. First  approach sounds good to me - consistent, and probably safe enough to infer that the user actually means `[]`. I'm looking into it now.
